proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6251 dākṣiṇa specifically gives Prakrit dāhiṇa/ḍāhiṇa ‘right’, Old Awadhi dā̆hina, Hindi dā̆hinā and Braj dahino, plus Hindi dā̃yā explained by crossing with vāma ‘left’. The h-bearing and contracted y-forms therefore belong to this long-vowel derivative rather than automatically to bare dakṣiṇa; local vowels, endings and loss of nasalization are qualified. No specific contact donor is established.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11533 vāma gives Kumaoni bāyõ, Old Awadhi bāeṁ ‘on the left’, Hindi bāyā̃ and Oriya bāyā̃ ‘pertaining to the left’. These y-bearing forms fit loss of intervocalic m with variable nasalization and v→b; unmarked nasalization and local final vowels remain qualified. Retained-m bama/bāmā and the h-bearing behiya are not silently grouped here.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 248.2 *adhiṣṭāt (remodelled after upariṣṭāt) gives Pali heṭṭhā, Prakrit heṭṭha/hiṭṭha ‘below’, Bhojpuri heṭhā̃, Old Awadhi heṭha, Gujarati heṭhe and Marathi heṭ. The survey’s loss of aspiration and varying gemination fit a qualified regional continuation of this specific second branch, not undifferentiated adhastāt.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 13401.1 siddha lists Sindhi sidho, Hindi sīdhā and Gujarati sīdhũ in the straight/upright family; Platts s.v. sīdhā explicitly supplies the right-hand sense and its Prakrit siddhao formation. Loss of aspiration and Nimadi t/d variation remain qualified; sudo/huda may involve a different clean/straight family and are excluded.
